conventions.convention: Distribution pairings are complex bilinear; tempered distributions are continuous complex-linear functionals on Schwartz space.
The Hilbert pairing is linear in its second variable: ⟨u,v⟩₂=(v,u)₁. Tensor completions retain the supplier's norm while conjugating its first-variable-linear pairing.

Fock sectors start at n=0, with zeroth tensor power and vacuum sector equal to C. Creation inserts the new vector first and multiplies the permutation projection by √(n+1); annihilation contracts the first factor and multiplies by √n.
Countable Choice is assumed for the tensor/Fock construction and all assigned results; no physical statistics assignment follows from choosing symmetric or antisymmetric sectors.

Bosonic ladder operators use maximal sector square-summability domains; their CCR are asserted on the common invariant finite-particle domain. Fermionic operators are bounded and their CAR hold on the whole Fock space.
The Hermite graph-core lemma uses the first-variable-linear Lebesgue L2 pairing and maximal position domain D(Q)={f:xf∈L2}.
Product-L2 identification uses the completed product measure. For second quantization, the one-factor measure remains μ, products with n≥2 are completed, and the vacuum is a singleton of unit mass.
The Segal field is (a†(h)+a(h))/√2. Weyl multiplication has phase exp(−i Im⟨h,k⟩₂/2), vacuum expectation exp(−‖h‖²/4), and derivative iΦ(h).

load_bearing.statement: Assuming Countable Choice, defines Schwartz tests, compactly supported smooth tests, tempered distributions, second-variable-linear Hilbert pairings, completed symmetric and antisymmetric tensor sectors, their square-summable Fock sums, vacuum, finite-particle subspace, and sector creation/contraction maps.

Under Countable Choice, for a separable complex Hilbert space with the second-variable-linear convention, both Fock sums are Hilbert spaces and the finite-particle subspace is dense. The maximal bosonic sector maps are closed, mutually adjoint, have that subspace as a graph core, and satisfy the displayed CCR there. Fermionic maps are bounded on the whole Fock space, have norms ‖h‖, and satisfy the displayed CAR there.

Under Countable Choice, for separable complex H, the finite-particle Segal field (a†(h)+a(h))/√2 is essentially self-adjoint for h≠0, with the stated maximal position-multiplier domain after one-mode/Hermite identification; h=0 closes to zero everywhere. The displayed exponential-vector formula defines strongly continuous Weyl unitaries satisfying the stated phase and vacuum Gaussian. W(th) has a norm derivative at zero exactly on D(Φ(h)), equal to iΦ(h).

Under Countable Choice, for sigma-finite (X,A,μ) and a finite-valued measurable vector ω:X→R^d, the sector-sum coordinate multipliers are self-adjoint on the displayed maximal square-integrability domains, with finite-particle domain intersections as graph cores. Their joint PVM is multiplication by indicators of sector-sum inverse images. The phase multipliers form strongly continuous unitary groups whose derivative domains are exactly the corresponding maximal multiplier domains; the vacuum has joint value zero.

Under Countable Choice, for complex Hilbert H, a unit vector e and K=e⊥, the maps Jₖ,ₘ=√binomial(k+m,k) Pₛ,ₖ₊ₘ(e⊗k⊗·) extend to a unitary Fₛ(Ce)⊗̂Fₛ(K)→Fₛ(H). Creation and annihilation by e become the one-mode ladder maps on the first factor on finite-particle vectors.

Under Countable Choice, for two sigma-finite measure spaces there is a unique unitary from the Hilbert tensor product of their complex L2 spaces onto L2 of their completed product measure, sending f⊗g to f(x)g(y) almost everywhere.
Under Countable Choice, Qf(x)=xf(x) on D(Q)={f∈L2(R):xf∈L2(R)} is self-adjoint, and the finite linear span of the oscillator Hermite functions is dense in D(Q) for the graph norm.

concerns.concern: Proof step 2.1 says adjoint testing forces the sector-(n+1) coordinate to be “a_{n+1}^\dagger(h)\Phi_n”. The Statement defines a_m† as creation restricted to input sector m, so this expression has the wrong input type; the required coordinate is a_n†(h)Φ_n. The surrounding sector-adjoint calculation supports that immediate index correction.
